decisions.issues: Minor, retouch if possible: the two palanquins seen through the gate stand on small wheels under their carrying poles (about x 0.22-0.30, y 0.75-0.82). Palanquins are carried, and in 1.2 and 1.5 they rest on legs. The guards carry spears as well as their swords and round shields. Otherwise clean: dusk estate, gatehouse, Nair guards watching the road, a servant lighting wall-niche lamps, road dust and the jackfruit tree. No text. The wide quiet dusk sky across the top has room for the long caption.

Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not the bible's side knot above the LEFT ear. Otherwise he follows the private-visit look: bare-headed, no turban, crest or spear, the V13 face and moustache, gold necklaces, a cream and gold mundu. He also has a gold-bordered shoulder cloth. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun with no flowers, white sari with a narrow gold border, gold ear studs. The Prince, about ten, wears a white mundu, a thin gold chain and a small topknot. Ornate and plainer palanquins rest on legs, which is right. The sky above the gate at the upper left has room for the caption.

Minor background details: three palanquins appear beyond the gate opening rather than two just inside it, and Padmini shows little grey threading. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet and stands on the verandah above the steps: old Kerala drape with no blouse, a white and gold sari, jasmine in her hair, a gold chain, walking stick in hand. She has a set face and looks off-panel left across the courtyard. The open dusk sky between the jackfruit tree and the roof has room for both balloons.

Minor background-only issues: the two palanquins beyond the gateway look like they sit on small wheels rather than being set down on their poles, and the gate guards hold spears with their round shields rather than swords. Both are small, far back, and do not affect the beat. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch17 bible row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, cream tunic with broad red sash, cream trousers, barefoot, no talwar. He is caught half-turned under the jackfruit tree in deep shade, glancing back over his shoulder, with one bare foot on the side path. Hands and feet are sound and there is no painted text. Clear dusk sky over the gatehouse (upper middle, about x 0.55 to 0.95, y 0.03 to 0.18) leaves room for his balloon without covering his face.

Continuity with 1.3 is weak. Padmini stands at courtyard level beside the foot of the verandah plinth instead of up on the verandah. She looks right toward the house, where in 1.3 she looks left across the courtyard toward the tree where Nagoji is, and her pose has a slight forward lean. Otherwise this is the closest likeness to her sheet on the page: deep-lined stern face, gold bead chain, ball ear studs, jasmine at a nape coil with grey threading, old drape with no blouse, stick in hand. Lit lamp niches are behind her, the palanquins rest on legs inside the gate, and there is no text. The dusk sky at the upper left and centre has room for the balloon.

Minor only. The King kneels at the foot of the steps, not on them, and his hands are on Padmini's feet. His hair has a few grey-looking highlight strands, and the knot sits toward the back of the head. Padmini's grey is a little heavier than a light threading. The gate guards carry spears and shields where the script asks for swords. Nagoji matches the sheet: turban, tunic, red sash, barefoot, moustache, clean chin and gold stud. Lettering: put the Varma balloon in the sky gap between the jackfruit foliage and the roof (upper middle), and the caption on the clear courtyard floor at bottom left or along the top-left edge.

Clean. Padmini is on the verandah with jasmine, gold chain, the blouseless Kerala drape and her stick, looking down past the King. The King is seen from behind, bare-headed with his knot on his left side, wearing the pearl drop earring, bead necklace and gold-bordered mundu with shoulder cloth. The Rani has a severe bun with no flowers, small gold studs and a white sari with a gold border. The Prince is coming up the steps in his mundu with a thin chain and topknot. The forehead mark from the sheet is not visible at this distance. Clear sky in the upper centre and the roof eaves at upper right leave room for both balloons.

Acceptable with minor issues. The close-up of the Prince matches his sheet: white forehead mark, thin gold chain, bare-chested, topknot, watchful frown. Two small problems. His curls are looser than the sheet's neat topknot, and the ear studs he wears in 2.2 and 2.4 are missing here. He also looks screen-left here but screen-right toward Nagoji in 2.4, a mild flip in screen direction. Nagoji is correctly off-panel to the upper left. Wide clear sunset sky across the upper left takes both balloons.

Acceptable. This is a low-angle two-shot with the boy looking up and Nagoji looking down. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down (brand hidden), broad red sash, cream trousers and long curly black hair. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush gold stud, and his feet are out of frame. His expression is a touch stern rather than gently serious. Hands are sound. The Prince's forehead mark from the sheet does not show at this angle. Open dusk sky between the tree and Nagoji's head, plus the leaves at upper left, gives room for three balloons.

Minor only. The King is smiling openly rather than hiding his amusement. The Rani and the King wear a white forehead namam that is not on their sheets, though it matches the Prince's. The gate guards are in back view. The ornament along the palanquin valance is decorative, not lettering. The Rani's hand is reaching his shoulder and her fingers are sound. Lettering: put the two Prince balloons in the sky gap above and right of his head, between the tree and the roof, or in the upper left above the gatehouse roof.

Minor only. The Rani's hair has a faint grey sheen not on her sheet. Clear sky above the centre is limited, so the two Rani balloons may need to sit over the upper-left foliage and gate roof, with the caption on the open earth at lower left. Faces and the hand on the shoulder stay clear. Otherwise clean: hand on the Prince's shoulder, both looking off right toward Nagoji, the Prince matches his sheet (forehead mark, topknot, chain), and the courtyard, gate, guards and dusk match 2.5.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch17 bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, no talwar. His forearm is sleeved, so the scar does not show, and his feet are out of frame. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun with no jasmine, small gold ear ornament, white sari with a narrow gold border, upright, hands clasped. The two face each other in profile, cool and measured, as the beat asks. The setting is the estate courtyard with the laterite gate, Nair guards with round shields, palanquins, lamps in the wall niches, the jackfruit tree and the verandah steps, so it matches panels 3.1 and 3.3. Clean. Nagoji inclines his head with his hands clasped, and the Rani is already turning away toward the verandah steps and the house. Nagoji is in the commander look, barefoot, with a clean-shaven chin under a curled moustache and a small gold stud. The white scar shows on his LEFT forearm, the correct side, and the brand is not legible. The Rani matches her sheet (no flowers, no mark). The courtyard and dusk light continue from 3.1. Open sky at upper centre takes both balloons.

The staging and setting of v01 are excellent: carved elephant and yali pillars, latticed eaves, a black mirror floor with lamp reflections, the storeroom doorway with clay vessels, the sky square at the top, all six principals and Nagoji apart, barefoot and correct. But Padmini does not match her sheet or the bible row. Her hair is silver, salt-and-pepper grey rather than thick black with a light threading of grey (the prompt explicitly says BLACK), and her face is gaunt and elderly, unlike the full, strong face she has on her sheet and in 1.3 and 2.2 on the verandah. Lesser drift: the Prince has lost the white forehead mark he wears on his sheet and in 3.1. Ramayyan wears a gold ear stud not on his sheet and is fully lit rather than half in shadow.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: the same raised corner view across the nalukettu, with the sunken court corner in the foreground and the square of evening sky at the top kept low-detail for captions. Keep the carved teak corner pillars with yalis and elephant processions, the latticed ventilation screens, the black oxide floor mirroring the lamps, the open doorway at right onto the dim storeroom of tall clay rice vessels, and every figure's place and pose. Fix Padmini Amma (seated centre right, jasmine, walking stick leaning beside her). She must have the face from her sheet and the verandah panels: a full, strong, broad face in her fifties, with heavy brows, deep lines at the eyes and mouth, and THICK BLACK hair coiled at the nape with fresh jasmine, with at most a few faint grey threads. No silver, white or salt-and-pepper hair, and not a thin, elderly face. Give the Prince the white vertical forehead mark and curly hair in a small neat topknot from his sheet. Draw Ramayyan with no earring and place him half in shadow at the edge of the lamplight, still holding the palm-leaf bundle and stylus.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the King's hair knot sits at the back of the crown rather than clearly above the LEFT ear (the same placement on 4.2 and 4.3, so it is consistent across the page). Otherwise clean: King on a low stool looking up and to the right, amused; Prince on a stool beside him in the same hands-on-knees posture, white mundu, thin gold chain, topknot; courtyard, lamps and storeroom doorway match the setting; roof and sky band at the top takes the three balloons. Nagoji is off-panel up and to the right, where the King is looking.

Minor: the King is standing here, though he was seated on his stool in 4.1 (it reads as him rising to look around), and he wears a gold-bordered upper cloth over one shoulder that 4.1 lacks. Minor: the low door in the storeroom's far corner is a little more visible than 'barely visible' and has a ring handle. A few woven sacks sit on the storeroom floor. Clean. Muted lamp-brown flashback palette with soft irregular edges. Young Varma, gaunt and wide-eyed, with matted hair and a torn dark-brown waist-cloth, no gold, crouches knees-up between clay grain jars. The scene has straw-bound paddy bundles, a woven mat, cobwebs, low beams and slits of light through the plank floor above, with no burlap sacks and no lamp. The low-detail earth wall and ceiling area above and right of the boy takes the off-panel balloon. The tail runs to the top edge, toward the present-day King above.

Minor: the bowl of rice reads as untouched with a few stray grains on the mat, but the 'pushed away' gesture is only implied by its placement at the mat's edge. Everything else is clean. It has three separate torn-edge slivers in the muted lamp-brown memory palette. The guard's hands drop gold fanams onto his palm, the anatomy is sound, the coins carry no markings and his sword hilt is at his waist. A barefoot figure in a mundu and red sash holds a drawn blade on a moonlit laterite-walled road, seen from behind with no face showing. There is no text, blood or anachronism, and a wide plain parchment band across the top holds both off-panel Varma balloons.

Minor: the boy reads nearer ten than seven, and he wears a pale grimy cloth over his shoulders, where 4.4 showed a gaunt, bare-chested boy in a dark-brown waist-cloth. The gaps in the floor are wider than slits, so the retainers' legs and feet show through, but this reads clearly as feet crossing overhead. The beat is right: a low angle from below, the plank floor, dust in the light, both hands pressed over his mouth, and an earth-walled cellar with jars and paddy bundles. There is no text. Clear space for both off-panel balloons is in the dark planks at upper left (x 0-0.35, y 0-0.3) and on the bare earth wall (x 0.4-0.75, y 0.42-0.6).

Minor: the palette is warm full colour rather than the muted lamp-brown memory palette of 5.1. Young Padmini's white sari has a gold border instead of being plain. Every beat is present: the storeroom, the clay vessels, the post, one torch held by a retainer, retainers with swords and round shields, and an older grey-haired leader with gold earrings and his sword drawn. A knife is held against the throat of the bare-chested husband pinned at the post, with no blood. Young Padmini, unlined, with black hair coiled with jasmine, stands empty-handed facing the leader, and the swaddled infant sleeps in a cloth cradle seen through the doorway. There is no cup and no text, and the hands are sound. Space for the off-panel balloon is on the dark wall above the doorway (x 0.3-0.55, y 0-0.1).

Minor only. The Prince's curly hair is fuller than a 'small neat topknot', though it is gathered into a knot on top. Varma matches his sheet closely: black side knot behind the left ear, pearl ear drop, curled moustache, beaded gold necklaces, cream mundu with a gold border, bare-chested and bare-headed. The setting (nalukettu courtyard, carved elephant pillars, open-wick brass lamps, black mirror floor, evening sky) matches panels 5.4 and 5.5. There is no painted text, and the stools and hands are sound. Varma's short balloon can sit in the open sky and roof area at the top centre (x 0.25 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.15), clear of both faces.

Inset continuity flaw, accepted because the inset is small and soft-edged: the Pillamar leader in the lower-right inset has a full black beard and dark hair, is seated and carries no sword. That contradicts the grey-haired, beardless, standing leader of 5.2. Young Padmini in the inset wears a red bindi and looks a little older than in 5.2. The main figure is strong: present-day Padmini matches her sheet closely (heavy brows, black hair threaded with grey, coiled with jasmine, gold stud and chain, cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse, walking stick), with a dry, stern expression. The courtyard matches 5.3 and 5.5, the hands are sound and there is no text. The roof and lattice at upper right (x 0.47-0.9, y 0-0.35) give clear room for three balloons away from the inset.

Minor: Varma wears a gold-bordered cream cloth over one shoulder, where the private-scene look is fully bare-chested, and his forehead carries namam lines. The rest is correct. His hair is gathered in a knot behind his left ear, consistent with page 4. His sheet face, curled moustache, pearl ear drop and gold necklaces all match. His smile is a knowing smirk, with eyes that stay guarded. Padmini, on the left, watches him and matches her sheet, with her walking stick. The pair are seated in the same nalukettu courtyard as 5.3 and 5.4. The hands, including Varma's clasped hands, are sound, and there is no text. Minor only. Padmini stands with her stick in hand, while she is seated in 5.5 and 7.2 (the prompt allows the stick in hand). Nagoji is drawn as sharply as Padmini rather than out of focus. His ear ornament is a tiny round gold bead that hangs very slightly; at print size it reads as a stud. Faint shading on his chin, but no beard. The face, moustache, commander costume, bare feet, the hand at the sash and the turning head all match. Varma is off panel to the right, where Padmini is looking. The top band of roof and sky has room for all three balloons.

Minor: Varma turns and looks to image left, toward an off-panel Nagoji, while panel 6.4 places Nagoji to the right of the seated King. The screen direction flips, but panel 6.3 sits between them, so it can stand. Otherwise the panel is clean. Varma's face matches his sheet: black hair, side knot above the left ear, pearl earrings, bare-chested, cream gold-bordered mundu, gold bead necklaces, no turban and no spear. He twists on a low stool with a stern, unplayful look. The setting is the nalukettu courtyard: carved yali and elephant pillar, lattice eaves, black mirror floor, rice jars, open-wick brass lamps. Hands are sound and there is no text. The roof and sky at upper right have room for the two Varma balloons, and the eaves and pillar at upper left can take Nagoji's short off-panel line.

None significant. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding hair with curly sides, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead mark or sacred thread. His arms are folded over the palm-leaf bundle, with the stylus in hand. He is lit fairly evenly rather than standing at the edge of the lamplight. The upper right sky and roof leave ample room for the balloon.

Clean. On a stool, the King leans forward with elbows on knees and hands clasped under his chin. He is bare-headed with a side knot above the left ear, black hair, pearl earrings, bare-chested, in a cream gold-bordered mundu with gold necklaces. The Prince beside him also leans forward, elbows on knees: about ten, white mundu, bare-chested, thin gold chain, topknot. Nagoji stands at right. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and jaw, a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe and long curly black hair. He wears a rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers, is barefoot and carries no talwar. A thread of smoke from a brass floor lamp drifts sideways toward Nagoji. The room, lighting and lamps match panel 6.2. There is no text, and hands and anatomy are sound. The roof tiles and lattice eaves across the upper middle, between the King and Nagoji, have room for three Varma balloons.

Minor. Both men stand, while the King is seated in 6.4 and 7.1. Varma adds gold armlets, a gold belt and a gold-bordered shoulder cloth not seen in 6.2 and 6.4, though the shoulder cloth also appears in 5.5 and 7.2. His hairline is high, but his face, moustache, pearl ear drop and black hair knot match his sheet. Ramayyan holds out a single rolled leaf tied with saffron thread, with no script on it. The King's hands stay at his sides and his sideways look is dry. Hands are sound. The sky, roof and lattice between the two heads leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. Varma's look is a sceptical sidelong frown more than glittering amusement. His knot sits at the crown toward the left rather than clearly above the left ear. Ramayyan holds his stylus while his fingers rest at the saffron knot, so 'loosening' is implied rather than explicit. The setting is the lamplit nalukettu with its black floor. The roof and sky band across the top (x 0.15-0.62, y 0-0.2) leaves room for both balloons.

The only candidate (v01) fails the likeness rules. Marthanda Varma's hair is heavily grey at the temples and sides, which breaks his MUST MATCH line ('black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure') and clashes with his black hair in 7.1. His knot is a bun at the back of the head, not a side knot above the left ear. Padmini's hair reads as mostly grey instead of thick black with light grey threading. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a flush stud. Nagoji also stands, while every following panel on the page shows him seated. The composition, the Rani's plate (cloth, lit lamp, ivory elephant with gold tusk), the Prince, Ramayyan and the setting all work.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact wide composition, courtyard, evening lamplight, the Rani with her silver plate and the folded cloth, lit lamp and ivory elephant, and the Prince and Ramayyan as drawn, but fix these likeness errors. Marthanda Varma's hair must be entirely jet BLACK with no grey or silver anywhere at the temples, sides or knot, exactly as in the previous panel. Gather it in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not a bun at the back of the head. Padmini Amma's hair must read as thick BLACK hair with only a few fine grey threads, not a grey or salt-and-pepper head, still coiled at the nape with fresh jasmine. Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging below it. For continuity with the next panels, where Padmini rises and goes to him, show Nagoji seated on the low stone step at the left edge of the court rather than standing: same rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers, barefoot. Keep the dark tiled roof and sky to the right of Varma's head clear for two balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's chin shows a faint shadow of texture but reads as clean-shaven. Minor only. Padmini's hands look somewhat older than her fifties. Her upper hand's fingers wrap under his wrist in a slightly tangled way but still read. Otherwise the beat is clean. The upper-left sleeve and upper-centre background (x 0.0-0.65, y 0.0-0.3) take both balloons.

Minor only: close-up so Padmini's walking stick is out of frame; Nagoji is seen from behind (turban, gold stud, curly hair consistent). Grip on his LEFT wrist with brand and white scar on the inner forearm, Padmini's wet eyes, jasmine, black hair with grey, gold chain, Kerala drape with no blouse all correct. Lettering space over the roof and sky at top centre and the lattice at top left.

Minor: a small maroon patch shows at Padmini's chest under the sari edge (reads as shadowed inner cloth, no sleeves); her walking stick is not shown. Otherwise strong: wide strip, Nagoji leaning back as if pulling away, she kisses the scarred inner left wrist, black mirror floor reflects both, turban on (correct before 8.4), clean chin and ear stud, storeroom jars and carved pillars match the setting. No text needed.

Minor issues only. Her hair shows rather more grey streaking than a light threading. Unlike the kneeling 8.2, she is now standing with her stick, which reads as her having risen. The beat is clear: eyes wet with a visible tear, face set like iron, head turning to her left toward the King off-panel. She matches her sheet, with jasmine, gold chain, Kerala drape and stick, in the same lamplit nalukettu. The dusk sky, roof and lattice at upper right and upper centre leave room for both balloons.

Minor: Padmini has a thin white sandal-paste line on her forehead that is not on her sheet or in 8.1/8.2 (small, not an identity break). Minor only. Varma's knot sits at the crown/back rather than clearly above the left ear. Minor only: Varma's knot sits at the upper back of the head (as on his sheet) rather than squarely above the left ear, and he wears a small gold drop rather than a pearl; the King holds an ordinary storeroom door rather than a low cellar door. Otherwise clean: Nagoji bare-headed with curled moustache, clean chin, flush ear stud, turban folded in his right hand, brand and white scar on the inner left forearm; Padmini (jasmine, grey threading, stick) with her hand on his forearm looking up; Rani in white, no flowers, glancing back from the storeroom doorway; Prince hesitating on the threshold. Minor: Padmini has moved to Nagoji's left side (she was at his right in 9.2), though the turban stays in his right hand and the brand on his inner left forearm is consistent; Ramayyan wears a thin gold neck chain (not a sacred thread); Nagoji gazes past Padmini rather than down at her. Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits at the crown/back rather than clearly above the left ear, and he wears a white-and-red forehead namam that 9.1 does not show. The beat is correct: the Prince comes out of the storeroom first with wide eyes and dusty knees, and the King follows with a hand on the boy's shoulder, holding out the red-cloth bundle. The conch is engraved on the IVORY GRIP, but the script and the 9.6 inset put it on the steel near the hilt. That makes the prop inconsistent and spoils the inset's reveal. The brand on Nagoji's forearm is a crisp, dark, tattoo-like spiral glyph with a tail, which reads as a logo or emblem, not the pale, puckered, blurred brand in the bible. The rest works: bare-headed, hair loose, cream tunic and red sash, clean chin, ear stud, dagger catching the lamplight, red cloth falling across his lap with the dark sheath beside it, and a low-detail lower corner.
decisions.correction: The ivory grip is plain, smooth polished ivory with gold fittings at guard and pommel and NO engraving, carving or symbol on it. The small conch outline belongs only on the steel just above the guard (it is revealed in the inset 9.6), so keep it tiny or out of view here. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm must be a pale, puckered, irregular patch of raised scar ridges blurred past reading, beside the long thin white scar. It must not be a crisp dark tattoo, spiral, swirl, circle or emblem of any kind. Keep everything else as drawn: Nagoji bare-headed with long curly hair loose, cream tunic and broad red sash, seated in the lamplit courtyard, the straight dagger raised in one hand catching the lamplight, the red cloth falling open across his lap and the plain dark wooden sheath in his other hand, the low-detail lower corner for the inset and the quiet roof shadow above for two speeches.

decisions.issues: Minor: a small near-black, faintly navy sleeve edge shows in the extreme lower-left corner where his cream tunic sleeve should be; at inset size it reads as shadow. Otherwise clean: tight inset of his right hand closing round the ivory grip with gold beaded guard and pommel matching 9.5's knife design, a plain unlettered conch outline struck into the steel near the hilt, left hand on the red cloth with the brand and scar on the inner left forearm, no painted text. Nagoji is the POV owner behind the camera (tail to bottom edge); Varma is off panel in front of him (tail to top edge); dark lamplit background upper centre-right holds both balloons.

Minor only. The brand on his raised LEFT forearm is a small, crisp reddish spiral near the elbow, not a pale ridged patch a hand's width above the wrist. At wide-shot scale it does not read as lettering. The knife grip reads brass/dark rather than the ivory of 9.5, which is negligible at this size.
